title: I built a free times tables game for my daughter with Claude Code and a local AI art pipeline. It actually worked.
author: photonenwerk-com
selftext:
This started as a project for my own kids. My daughter urgently needed to practice her times tables. I tried a few ready-made apps first, but they were full of ads and I wasn't happy with any of them. So I sat down with a few AI agents and built her a game.

It actually worked. She went from "we really need to practice" to the top of her class, and she has earned the title "math queen". n=1, I know, and she did the practicing, not the app. But it was enough for me to polish it and put it out for free: no ads, no in-app purchases, no tracking, works offline, 5 languages, browser, Android and iOS.

You tap the answer on a 10x10 number board. Every times table you master unlocks an animal and its habitat, later baby animals hatch. Under the hood there's spaced repetition, difficulty that adapts to the kid, and division introduced as the reverse of each multiplication.

**How it was made**

Day 1 was a Godot prototype, written almost entirely by agents in OpenCode, mostly DeepSeek Flash with a bit of GPT. It was playable that evening. On day 2 the agent ported it to plain HTML/JS. A number board doesn't need an engine, and one small web build now runs as a PWA, an Android WebView app and an iOS app.

Since day 3 nearly all the work has been done with Claude Code (Opus 5.5): the second version of the learning path, the tests, the Android/iOS wrapper, store listings via the Play and App Store APIs, and the promo tooling. I write the spec, make the decisions and review. My kids are the QA team. About 115 commits in seven weeks.

**Art:** everything is generated locally on my own GPU in ComfyUI with Krea 2 Turbo; stickers get their background removed with BiRefNet + SDMatte. Two things kept it from looking random. Every prompt contains the same style string (storybook gouache, thick clean outlines, warm colors). And each animal has exactly one description that goes into both its sticker prompt and its habitat background, so the cow has the same patches in both. Every image is a DVC pipeline stage with a fixed prompt and seed, so `dvc repro` rebuilds the exact asset, and changing an animal's description regenerates sticker and background together. That's about 60 images: 16 animals, 11 baby animals, 28 backgrounds, rank badges and the icon.

**Sound:** Stable Audio Open, also local. A script renders 5 seeds per sound, trims and normalizes them and builds a small listening page. I pick by ear, the seed goes into the pipeline. The UI click is from Kenney (CC0). The game has no music; the music in the video is Suno.

**The video** wasn't recorded by hand. A script plays the game in headless Chrome through a small control API (it gets every 7th task wrong on purpose, so you see the help), records the screencast, logs every sound the game plays with its timestamp, and ffmpeg mixes it all. One command renders every language and the App Store preview cuts.

**What I'd do again:** keep every generated asset reproducible. I regenerated far more often than I expected. And let agents do the plumbing (builds, store APIs, wrappers, tests), while I spend my own time watching the kids play: when they get bored, frustrated or stuck is something no model told me.

Free on web, Android and iOS: [https://photonenwerk.com/games/learning/1x1/en/?auto&utm\_source=reddit](https://photonenwerk.com/games/learning/1x1/en/?auto&utm_source=reddit) (on a phone it forwards to the store after 3 seconds)

Happy to answer questions about the pipeline or the learning logic.
